title: DTLS: Don't check legacy record version in dissect_dtls
description:
dissect_dtls_heur() always calls looks_like_dtls(), and, unlike
TLS, we don't call conversation_set_dissector_from_frame_number,
so if we call dissect_dtls() either it already looks like DTLS,
or else the dissector was set to DTLS via some other method (e.g.
port, Decode As.)

Unlike TLS, we call the same dissector for all versions of DTLS,
and unlike TLS over TCP segments, we don't expect Continuation Data
over UDP datagrams. In any case, dissect_dtls_record() always checks
the content type and marks Continuation Data if it's unknown, which
means that the only thing calling looks_like_dtls() in dissect_dtls()
does is check the legacy_record_version *if* the session version hasn't
set yet (so generally on the first pass) but *also* we didn't get here
from the heuristic dissector *and* the content type is valid.

As RFC 9147 indicates that the legacy_record_version MUST be ignored
for all purposes, it's fine to ignore it (other than perhaps a future
expert info item) and dissector according to the record type at this point.

Related to #19808
